newsitem.title: BELGIUM: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 123 AT WORLD CUP TIE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BELGIAN POLICE DETAIN 123 AT WORLD CUP TIE.

text.p: Belgian police said on Saturday they had detained 123 football supporters before and during a World Cup clash between Belgium and the Netherlands which the Dutch side won 3-0.
"Of the 123, 92 are from the Netherlands. The rest are Belgian," police spokesman Michael Jonniaux said.
Thirteen of the arrests were likely to result in charges for carrying banned weapons, drugs possession, serious vandalism or wounding, he said.
Jonniaux said one Belgian was slightly hurt when he was punched in the face by a Dutchman.
Most of those who were detained before the game were released at 2000 GMT and escorted by police to the Dutch border.
Virtually all the arrests were made before the match. There were no incidents in the stadium during the game, he said.
Jonniaux said he expected no further problems during the night as most of the Dutch fans had already left Brussels by bus. The cold weather would also help prevent problems, he said.
Belgian police deployed more than 1,500 officers, 150 mounted policemen, water cannon and 20 dog teams throughout Brussels for the match.
The match was played at the Heysel stadium where 39 fans died after Liverpool supporters roited at the European Cup final against Juventus in 1985.
The stadium has since been rebuilt and renamed after former Belgian monarch King Baudouin, whose brother King Albert II watched the game.
